text:
IncidentBot: ALERT: sudden CPU spike on tokenizer pods in namespace 'inference'. 5 pods OOMKilled in last 3m. Severity: P2. Paging oncall.

Alex Chen: I'm on it, looking at metrics. seeing a big tail of prompt lengths around 1M tokens from a small number of requests.

Sara Patel: whoa, 1M tokens? must be a client bug or adversarial input. any immediate customer impact?

Alex Chen: yes, several routes returning 502/503 and token generation latencies > 30s. A few pods are in CrashLoopBackOff with "OOMKilled".

Joyce Rivera: taking pager. can you paste pod events + kernel OOM logs?

Alex Chen: running describe + logs:
```
kubectl -n inference describe pod tokenizer-5f7d8
Events:
  Type     Reason     Age                  From               Message
  ----     ------     ----                 ----               -------
  Warning  OOMKilling  2m (x3 over 2m)     kubelet, node-12    Memory cgroup out of memory: Kill process 4421 (tokenizer) score 123

kubectl -n inference logs tokenizer-5f7d8 -c tokenizer
[2026-03-15T01:12:01Z] Received prompt length: 1048576 tokens
[2026-03-15T01:12:02Z] Allocating tokenizer buffer: 2.0GB
[2026-03-15T01:12:03Z] Fatal: std::bad_alloc
```

Matt B: looks like tokenization path allocates O(n) memory per token and we hit a pathological case.

Katie Morgan: can we throttle max input length at the gateway while we triage? I can push a quick rule to reject > 200k tokens.

Alex Chen: +1, gateway rule would reduce blast radius. pushing a temporary ingress rule now.

ops-bot: deploy triggered: ingress/ratelimit-patch v1 -> v1-hotfix (by Katie Morgan) :rocket:

Alex Chen: ingress rule applied. blocking requests with token_count > 200000. Monitoring mem usage.

Joyce Rivera: marking incident channel, notifying CS. @Sara can you check which customers had requests >200k in last 10m and flag for outreach?

Sara Patel: on it. pulling request logs. initial quick scan: 3 tenant ids show spikes, two are internal test clients, one looks like customer "acme-ml" generating long debug dumps.

Liam Ross: I'll cordon node-12 where most OOM kills happened, drain low-priority pods to stabilize.

Alex Chen: kubectl cordon node-12 && kubectl drain node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force -n inference

IncidentBot: node-12 cordoned by Liam Ross at 1930054522

Alex Chen: after ingress rule + cordon, new OOMs stopped. memory for tokenizer pool back to normal. still seeing increased latency on some in-flight requests.

Joyce Rivera: handing off to oncall for overnight monitoring: @Liam you take second shift, I'll do initial postmortem doc. next oncall: Liam Ross.

Liam Ross: taking handoff. what's the follow-up checklist?

Alex Chen: follow-ups: 1) patch tokenizer to early-validate input token count + fail fast 2) add defensive caps in tokenization memory allocations 3) add an alert for >100k token inputs via telemetry 4) rate-limit per-tenant at gateway 5) postmortem and client outreach for Acme-ML.

Sara Patel: recorded impacted requests, saving logs to s3://redwood-incident-logs/1930054321/ for postmortem. customer impact: 503s for ~12 minutes for 1% of requests across the inference fleet.

Katie Morgan: rolling a canary tokenizer change that rejects >500k tokens in library, will do a quick smoke test in staging before prod.

Matt B: adding unit tests and a fuzz test for extreme prompt lengths. also evaluating smaller-memory parsing algorithm.

Joyce Rivera: writing initial incident summary and severity note. tagging support for outreach. will create postmortem ticket.

IncidentBot: Incident P2 opened: #INC-2026-1930054321, timeline started at 1930054321.

Alex Chen: final note: root cause = unbounded client-supplied prompt lengths hitting tokenizer's O(N) memory path. mitigations applied: ingress token cap, node cordon/drain, canary patch queued. next steps documented in ticket.

Joyce Rivera: closing slack incident thread for now, leave open for updates. please add any logs or timeline notes to the incident ticket. :white_check_mark:
